headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill aims to reduce residential utility bills by shifting the costs of grid infrastructure and capacity to large energy users, such as data centers.
supporters: Del. Destiny LeVere Bolling, State Senator Louise Lucas, Dominion Energy, Governor Spanberger
news_headline: Virginia Law Shifts Grid Costs to Large Energy Users
news_summary: Virginia's HB 1393, which became law in May 2026, aims to shift the costs of grid infrastructure and capacity procurement to large energy users, including data centers. This legislation is projected to save average residential customers approximately $5.52 per month by ensuring data centers pay their fair share for the grid demands they create.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates that water utilities report monthly water consumption by data centers to increase transparency regarding their water usage.
news_headline: Virginia Law Mandates Data Center Water Use Reporting
news_summary: A new Virginia law, effective January 1, 2027, requires water utilities to report monthly water consumption by data centers to the State Water Control Board. This legislation, identical to HB 496 and signed by the Governor, aims to increase transparency regarding data center water usage, which has been a point of public concern.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill requires new high-energy use facilities, including data centers, to undergo site assessments for sound profiles and allows localities to assess environmental impacts.
supporters: Del. Thomas, community advocates, Governor Spanberger
news_headline: Virginia Law Imposes Data Center Siting and Noise Assessments
news_summary: Virginia's HB 153, signed into law and effective July 1, 2026, mandates that new high-energy use facilities, including data centers, undergo site assessments for sound profiles impacting nearby residential areas and schools. The law also grants localities the power to require assessments of environmental and historical impacts before approving data center projects.
